account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment book: a morning market walk, lunch at home, town accounts at one, and now tea with my neighbour at the east-bank cottage. I counted 128 emeralds in the treasury and left them untouched. Neither the secretary nor I has located receipts or account ledgers, so the accounts remain incomplete; that is a gap to investigate, not evidence of wrongdoing.

The baker has been moving supplies and bread. Townsfolk reported seeing the baker carrying wheat at the bakery, and two reported a sack of bread at the inn. I saw the baker bringing bread to market and putting bread in the stall chest. This could all be ordinary bakery business; I do not know of any unusual gathering from firsthand evidence.

The most intriguing detail is the innkeeper's request to see me tomorrow at eighteen hundred in the great hall, explicitly arriving then and not early. I approved it and asked the secretary to enter it in the appointment book. I have not learned the purpose. The emphasis on not arriving early might mean something is being prepared, but I cannot yet say what, or who besides the innkeeper is involved.

The secretary confirmed today's tea directly with my neighbour, who was waiting when I arrived and has welcomed me warmly. My neighbour has asked for town news rather than disclosed anything unusual so far. I have a feeling something may be going on without me, but at present no evidence establishes a secret plan. I want to hear what my neighbour has actually seen or heard, and keep tomorrow's appointment punctually.
